question: Foreign share for the three top-150 recipients that file no Form 990 (Compassion International, OneHope, Convoy of Hope; $150.5m of FY2023-24 top-50 DAF inbound): read each one's FY2023-24 audited financial statements or ECFA profile for programme spending outside the US, and replace the [I] average-share imputation
conclusion_affected: Top-150 estimate ($1.868bn, 58.8% of inbound) treats these three as zero; the [I] extrapolation gives them the 61.7% average
rationale: Church-affiliated filers have no e-file 990, so no Part IX line 3 or Schedule F; they are 4.7% of top-150 inbound

question: Census instead of extrapolation: parse Form 990 Part IX lines 1-3, 25 and Schedule F Part I for the 5,268 remaining NTEE-Q or friends-of recipient EINs (ranks 151+; with 2 blank-EIN names, $1.369bn inbound) with the same script (--top 6000)
conclusion_affected: The [I] add-on of $0.937bn that lifts the combined share from 3.82% to 4.78% of total grants
rationale: The rank 101-150 share (61.6%) is close to the top-150 average (61.7%), but small Q organisations and friends-of bodies may differ; the script already supports a larger --top

question: Foreign spending by large non-Q recipients: run the same Schedule F Part I / line 3 parse on the 500 largest net Schedule I recipients of any NTEE code (e.g. Global Greengrants C12, Global Fund for Children A33Z, Partners In Health, Samaritan's Purse, universities with foreign campuses) to size DAF money reaching abroad outside the Q/friends frame
conclusion_affected: Whether 3.8-4.8% of total grants (direct + Q/friends pass-through) is a floor for DAF money reaching abroad
rationale: Two of the nine named intermediaries are not Q-coded, and relief/health NGOs coded E, X or P are outside the frame; their foreign spend is not counted

question: Test the proportional assumption with grant purpose text: for top-50 Schedule I lines to the top-150 recipients, classify the filed purpose text (e.g. 'Ukraine', 'Gaza', 'US programs', 'general support') and compare the implied foreign share of designated DAF dollars with the recipient-level expense share
conclusion_affected: Central estimate applies each recipient's average foreign expense share to DAF dollars; restricted DAF grants may differ
rationale: The estimate treats DAF money as fungible within the recipient; Schedule I purpose text is the only filed signal of donor designation

question: Schedule F under-reporting check: list top-150 recipient-years where Form 990 Part IV line 14b is Yes but Schedule F Part I reports $0 (e.g. American Israel Education Foundation, $28.8m inbound) or where Part I is far below Part IX line 3 (e.g. American Friends of Yeshiva Dmir), and read the Part V narrative and audited statements
conclusion_affected: Recipient-level foreign shares for about 10 recipients ($0.1bn inbound); filing-quality note for Schedule F Part I
rationale: 19 recipient-years report Part I non-investment spending below 95% of line 3; the expense measure uses the larger of the two, so Part I gaps matter only where line 3 is also zero
